title: Indians Top OECD Citizenship List Again: 9.25 Lakh in Five Years
excerpt: Indian citizens acquired more OECD citizenships than any other nationality between 2020 and 2024, with Canada, the US and Australia leading, the OECD's International Migration Outlook 2026 shows.
body:
• Around 9.25 lakh Indians acquired citizenship of an OECD member country between 2020 and 2024, the most of any nationality, according to the OECD's International Migration Outlook 2026.
  • The five-year total is up 41% from just over 6.5 lakh in 2015-2019, and Indians accounted for about 10% of the nearly 87 lakh people who became citizens of OECD countries in the period.
  • In 2024 alone, 2.30 lakh Indians took OECD citizenship, led by Canada (87,320), the United States (48,820) and Australia (28,969).
  • For diaspora readers: Canada naturalised 2.61 lakh Indians over the five years, up 150% on the previous period, making it the single biggest citizenship destination for Indians.

Indians remain the largest group of people taking up citizenship in the world's advanced economies. Around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens acquired the nationality of a member country of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) between 2020 and 2024, according to the OECD's International Migration Outlook 2026, released on Thursday and reported by The Times of India.

The figure is a sharp rise of 41% from just over 6.5 lakh Indians who acquired OECD citizenship during 2015-2019. India stayed ahead of Syria and Mexico, whose nationals accounted for around 5.9 lakh citizenship acquisitions each in OECD countries over the same five years. China ranked sixth, with its total falling nearly 12% to 3.4 lakh.

Canada leads the citizenship table

Canada accounted for the largest share of Indian naturalisations. A total of 2.61 lakh Indians became Canadian citizens during 2020-2024, an increase of 150% compared with the preceding five-year period. The report attributes the rise to the growth of Indian communities in several member countries, particularly Canada, where established communities have expanded the pool of residents eligible to apply for citizenship.

In 2024, the most recent year broken out in the data the OECD shared with The Times of India, 2.30 lakh Indians acquired OECD citizenship. Canada granted citizenship to 87,320 Indians that year, followed by the United States with 48,820 and Australia with 28,969. The 2023 total was marginally lower at nearly 2.25 lakh, with the same three countries accounting for most acquisitions.

One in ten new OECD citizens was Indian

Across all nationalities, OECD member countries took in nearly 87 lakh new citizens between 2020 and 2024, and Indians made up around 10% of them, the same share as in the previous five-year period, when about 65 lakh people in total acquired OECD citizenship. The OECD has 38 member countries, including the US, the UK, European nations, Australia, Canada, Japan and South Korea.

The wider report also records that around 30 lakh people acquired the nationality of an OECD country in 2025. The US accounted for almost 9 lakh of those new citizens, up 9% on 2024, followed by Germany and Spain with about 3 lakh each, while Canada ranked fourth after a 22% drop to nearly 3 lakh.

"Migration remains high, and immigrants now account for 16% of employment across the OECD. With ageing populations and slower productivity growth, countries cannot afford to waste the skills migrants bring."

— Mathias Cormann, OECD Secretary-General

New migration is slowing, even as citizenship rises

Citizenship numbers reflect settlement decisions made years earlier, and they are rising even as fresh migration cools. India remained the largest origin country of new migrants to OECD member countries in 2024, but the number of Indian migrants fell 19%, from 6.07 lakh in 2023 to 4.94 lakh in 2024.

Student flows are also easing. International student inflows to OECD countries fell from 19 lakh in 2024 to 16 lakh in 2025, with the decline concentrated in traditional English-speaking destinations, while European countries such as Austria, Germany and Italy continued to attract growing numbers. China and India remained the largest source countries, with 8.5 lakh Chinese students and 8.3 lakh Indian students in OECD countries. Indian students are also the largest group of foreign students in Germany, according to the OECD's Germany chapter of the same report.

What it means for the diaspora

For Indian families in Canada, the US, Australia and the UK, the numbers describe a community moving from temporary status to permanence: work permits and study visas first, permanent residence next, and citizenship as the final step. The full India findings were reported by The Times of India. Readers weighing naturalisation should check their own eligibility against their host country's residence rules, since citizenship acquisitions measure completed settlement, not a new application route.
